facts.statement: Lufengosaurus was a massospondylid dinosaur that lived in southwestern China during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus (, meaning "Lufeng lizard") is a genus of massospondylid dinosaur which lived during the Early Jurassic period in what is now southwestern China.

facts.statement: The first remains of Lufengosaurus were discovered in the late 1930s by geologist Bien Meinian in the Lower Lufeng Formation near Lufeng, Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: The first remains of Lufengosaurus were found during the late 1930s by geologist Bien Meinian in the Lower Lufeng Formation at Shawan, near Lufeng in the Yunnan Province of China.

facts.statement: C. C. Young named the type species Lufengosaurus huenei in 1940, deriving the genus name from the location Lufeng and the species name from his mentor Friedrich von Huene.
facts.quote: Young would go on to name the animal's type species, Lufengosaurus huenei, in 1940, with the generic name referring to Lufeng where it was found and the specific name honoring Young's old tutor, the German paleontologist Friedrich von Huene.

facts.statement: A second species, Lufengosaurus magnus, was named by Young in 1940 and fully described in 1947.
facts.quote: A second species of Lufengosaurus, L. magnus, was also named by Young in 1940 in the same paper as Lufengosaurus huenei and would be fully described by him in 1947.

facts.statement: Most authors consider L. magnus to be a junior synonym of L. huenei, representing larger individuals of the type species.
facts.quote: However, most authors have regarded it as a junior synonym of L. huenei, with its specimens being said to simply represent larger individuals of the type species.

facts.statement: In 2015, an international team led by Yao-Chang Lee discovered preserved collagen protein in a Lufengosaurus fossil.
facts.quote: In 2015, preserved collagen protein was found in a Lufengosaurus fossil by an international team led by Yao-Chang Lee of Taiwan's National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus is often described as a small early sauropodomorph approximately 6 meters long.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus is often described as a rather small early sauropodomorph, about 6 m long.

facts.statement: When including L. magnus specimens, Gregory S. Paul estimated a length of 9 meters and a weight of 1.7 metric tons in 2010, while Benson et al. estimated a mass of 2.3 tonnes in 2014.
facts.quote: However, when the L. magnus specimens are included, its size is more considerable: Gregory S. Paul estimated a length of 9 m and a weight of 1.7 MT in 2010, while Benson et al. (2014) estimated a mass of 2.3 tonnes.

facts.statement: Researchers inferred that Lufengosaurus was bipedal based on its long neck and relatively short forelimbs.
facts.quote: From these it was inferred that the species was bipedal, even before it became common to assume this for all basal sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype specimen is 25 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull of the holotype is 25 cm long.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus had a deep, broad snout with distinctive bony bumps behind its nostrils and on its cheeks.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus snout was deep and broad, and it had distinctive bony bumps just behind its large nostrils and on its cheeks.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus had closely spaced, serrated teeth suited for a leaf-based diet.
facts.quote: Its closely spaced, serrated teeth suited a diet of leaves.

facts.statement: About thirty major specimens of Lufengosaurus have been discovered, including juvenile individuals.
facts.quote: About thirty major specimens have been discovered, including those of juveniles.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus was herbivorous despite possessing sharp claws, including a large thumb claw.
facts.quote: It was herbivorous, although it had sharp claws (with an especially large thumb claw) and teeth.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Lufengosaurus was partially omnivorous based on its sharp claws and teeth, though its teeth resemble those of herbivorous iguanian lizards.
facts.quote: These features have been used to support claims, the most recent by Cooper in 1981, that Lufengosaurus may have been at least partially omnivorous, but the sharp teeth witnessed in Lufengosaurus and other early sauropodomorphs are similar to those seen in iguanaian lizards – which are herbivorous.

facts.statement: Young originally assigned Lufengosaurus to the family Plateosauridae within the suborder Prosauropoda.
facts.quote: Young originally assigned Lufengosaurus to the Plateosauridae of the suborder Prosauropoda, noting that it stood close to Plateosaurus fraasianus.

facts.statement: While sometimes considered a member of Plateosauridae, some cladistic analyses classify Lufengosaurus as a member of Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: It is still sometimes considered a member of Plateosauridae, though some cladistic analyses have found it to be a member of Massospondylidae instead.

facts.statement: Of the three historically named species of Lufengosaurus, only L. huenei is almost universally considered valid today.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus has historically had a maximum of three named species, only one of these being almost unilaterally considered valid nowadays: L. huenei.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus lived approximately 203 to 191 million years ago during the Hettangian and Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico hace aproximadamente 203 y 191 millones de años, en el Hettangiense y el Pliensbachiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus is often described as a small early sauropodomorph measuring approximately 6 meters in length and nearly 3 meters in height.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus a menudo se describe como un sauropodomorfo temprano bastante pequeño, medía aproximadamente 6 metros de largo y casi 3 de alto.

facts.statement: More than 30 specimens of Lufengosaurus have been discovered.
facts.quote: Más de 30 especímenes han sido descubiertos.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Lufengosaurus magnus at 9 meters and a weight of 1.7 tonnes in 2010.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimó una longitud de 9 metros y un peso de 1,7 toneladas en 2010.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Lufengosaurus measures 25 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo del holotipo mide 25 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus had a long skull and widely spaced teeth.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus tenía un cráneo largo y sus dientes estaban ampliamente espaciados.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus had long, powerful hind legs and short arms.
facts.quote: Tenía largas y poderosas patas traseras y brazos cortos

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus possessed large claws, particularly a thumb claw that was sharp and curved like a sickle.
facts.quote: Las grandes garras, en especial la del pulgar que era afilada y curva en forma de hoz.

facts.statement: The snout of Lufengosaurus was deep and wide, featuring distinct bony protuberances just behind its large nasal openings and on its cheeks.
facts.quote: El hocico de Lufengosaurus era profundo y ancho, y tenía protuberancias óseas distintivas justo detrás de sus grandes fosas nasales y en sus mejillas.

facts.statement: In the late 1930s, geologist Bien Meinian began discovering fossils in Shawan, near Lufeng, in Yunnan province.
facts.quote: A fines de la década de 1930, el geólogo Bien Meinian comenzó a descubrir fósiles en Shawan, cerca de Lufeng, en la provincia de Yunnan.

facts.statement: In 1941, Yang named the remains of a 'prosaurpod' Lufengosaurus huenei.
facts.quote: En 1941, Yang nombró restos de un "prosaurópodo" Lufengosaurus huenei.

facts.statement: The holotype, IVPP V15, a partial skeleton, was found in the lower Lufeng Formation.
facts.quote: El holotipo , IVPP V15, un esqueleto parcial, se encontró en la Formación Lufeng inferior.

facts.statement: In 1958, a specimen of Lufengosaurus became the first complete dinosaur skeleton mounted in China.
facts.quote: En 1958, un ejemplar de Lufengosaurus fue el primer esqueleto completo de dinosaurio montado en China.

facts.statement: A commemorative 8-yuan postage stamp was issued on April 15, 1958, to celebrate the event, marking the first time a dinosaur was depicted on a stamp.
facts.quote: Se emitió un sello postal conmemorativo de 8 yuanes el 15 de abril de 1958 para celebrar el evento, la primera vez que se representaba un dinosaurio en un sello.

facts.statement: In 2015, an international team led by Yao-Chang Lee found preserved collagen protein in a Lufengosaurus fossil.
facts.quote: En 2015, un equipo internacional dirigido por Yao-Chang Lee, del Centro Nacional de Investigación de Radiación Sincrotrónica de Taiwán, encontró una proteína de colágeno preservada en un fósil de Lufengosaurus.

facts.statement: The formation where Lufengosaurus was found is now considered to date from the Early Jurassic, between the Hettangian and Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Originalmente considerada triásica, esta formación ahora se considera que data del Jurásico inferior entre el Hettangiense al Sinemuriense.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus lived from the Hettangian to the Bajocian, approximately 201.4 to 168.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Bajocian (201.4 to 168.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It was inferred that the species was bipedal, even before this was commonly assumed for all basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: De estos se infirió que la especie era bípeda, incluso antes de que fuera común asumir esto para todos los sauropodomorfos basales.

facts.statement: The diet of Lufengosaurus is a mystery; while assumed to be herbivorous, its small, spaced teeth had edges and could have been used to eat meat.
facts.quote: la dieta de este dinosaurio es un misterio se ha asumido que eran herbívoros, pero los dientes pequeños y espaciados tenían filo y pudieron usarse también para comer carne.

facts.statement: The sharp teeth seen in Lufengosaurus and other prosauropods were similar to those of the modern herbivorous iguana.
facts.quote: Pero los dientes agudos vistos en Lufengosaurus así como en otros prosaurópodos eran similares a los de la iguana moderna que es herbívora.

facts.statement: It is thought that Lufengosaurus used its thumb claw for defense or to strip leaves from trees.
facts.quote: Se piensa que la usaba en su defensa o para arrancar las hojas de los árboles.

facts.statement: Like all early sauropodomorphs, Lufengosaurus had much longer hind limbs than forelimbs and was probably bipedal.
facts.quote: Como todos los primeros sauropodomorfos, el Lufengosaurus tenía extremidades posteriores mucho más largas que las anteriores y probablemente era bípedo.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus was herbivorous, although it had sharp claws, including an especially large thumb nail.
facts.quote: Era herbívoro, aunque tenía garras afiladas, con una uña del pulgar especialmente grande y dientes.

facts.statement: These features have been used to support claims, most recently by Cooper in 1981, that Lufengosaurus may have been at least partially omnivorous.
facts.quote: Estas características se han utilizado para respaldar las afirmaciones, la más reciente de Cooper en 1981, de que Lufengosaurus pudo haber sido al menos parcialmente omnívoro

facts.statement: Embryos of this genus also represent the earliest evidence of soft tissue preservation in vertebrates.
facts.quote: Los embriones de este género también representan la evidencia más temprana de preservación de tejidos blandos de vertebrados.

facts.statement: Yang assigned Lufengosaurus to Plateosauridae, and this remains a common classification in China.
facts.quote: Yang asignó Lufengosaurus a Plateosauridae y esta sigue siendo una clasificación común en China.

facts.statement: Some cladistic analyses have found Lufengosaurus to be a member of Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Algunos análisis cladísticos han encontrado a Lufengosaurus como miembro de Massospondylidae.

facts.statement: New work has shown that Lufengosaurus was more closely related to Coloradisaurus and Massospondylus than to Plateosaurus.
facts.quote: Lufengosaurus estaba más cerca de Coloradisaurus y Massospondylus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Lufengosaurus is Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Massospondylidae

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus belongs to the family Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Family: Massospondylidae

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: In the West, Lufengosaurus magnus is often considered a modern synonym of Lufengosaurus huenei, representing large individuals.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en Occidente esto se considera a menudo un sinónimo más moderno de Lufengosaurus huenei, que representa individuos grandes.

facts.statement: However, the identity of Gyposaurus sinensis as Lufengosaurus is generally doubted today.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la identidad hoy se duda en general.

facts.statement: In 1981, Michael Cooper suggested that Lufengosaurus and Yunnanosaurus were species of the South African genus Massospondylus.
facts.quote: En 1981, Michael Cooper sugirió que Lufengosaurus y Yunnanosaurus eran especies del género sudafricano Massospondylus.

facts.statement: However, a new 2005 analysis by Paul Barrett and colleagues established Lufengosaurus huenei as a distinct genus separate from Massospondylus or Yunnanosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un nuevo análisis en 2005 por Paul Barrett y sus colegas del cráneo de Lufengosaurus huenei lo establece como un género distinto separado de Massospondylus o Yunnanosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers found preserved collagen protein in a Lufengosaurus fossil that was over 100 million years older than any previously recorded fossil protein.
facts.quote: En 2015, un equipo internacional dirigido por Yao-Chang Lee, del Centro Nacional de Investigación de Radiación Sincrotrónica de Taiwán, encontró una proteína de colágeno preservada en un fósil de Lufengosaurus. La proteína, descrita en Nature Communications de 31 de enero de 2017, tenía más de 100 millones de años más que cualquier proteína fósil previamente registrada.

facts.statement: Lufengosaurus was the first complete dinosaur skeleton mounted in China, commemorated by a 1958 postage stamp.
facts.quote: Fue el primer esqueleto completo montado en China, con una estampilla postal de 1958 conmemorando el suceso.
